$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x)
$$

Let $F(x)=6{x}^{2}+5x+1$ for $x\in [-1,1).$ The Fourier series of the $2$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=1$ and $f(x)=6{x}^{2}+5x+1$ for $x\in [-1,1).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{1}{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(6{x}^{2}+5x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[2{x}^{3}+\frac{5}{2}{x}^{2}+x]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(2+\frac{5}{2}+1)-((-2)+\frac{5}{2}+(-1)) \\  & =\frac{11}{2}-(-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
